solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Assumed extremely new floor should be included

indicators.note: the floor piece must be included, placed within the other letters

parts.note: extremely means too, as in too hot
to floor a boxer is to knock him out, KO

explanation.surface: Someone presumes a brand-new floor will be part of the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a role or quality is to assume it, so the phrasal verb in the past tense matches.

clue.text: Put into service uniform, is wearing hat upon commencement of duty

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit upon the last

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the hat is worn around the word is, so those letters go inside it

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
the first letter of duty

explanation.surface: A soldier is set to work, in uniform and hat, as the shift begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To utilise something is to make use of it, putting it into service.

clue.text: Maybe publishing revision of urban novel

indicators.note: a revision reworks the text, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor reworks a city-set novel before publication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Publishing' in 'publishing is fun' is a gerund, a verb used as a noun, which is why 'Maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A gerund such as publishing is the grammatical category called a verbal noun; it is one example among many.

clue.text: Hear a low-pitched shot somewhere in the East End

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Listen to a deep-toned gunshot somewhere in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' suggests a homophone, but it is part of the anagram fodder. The East End is the traditionally working-class eastern part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitechapel Road is a main street in Whitechapel, a district of London's East End, so it is one such place.

clue.text: Christian city in China

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old written abbreviation of Christian, using the Greek chi
second meaning: ..., the historic capital of Shaanxi province

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a single Chinese city with a Christian name; in fact the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The written contraction Xian, with X for the Greek letter chi, stands for Christian; Xi'an is the ancient Chinese capital famed for its terracotta army.

clue.text: Novel caught up in your outcry

indicators.note: the novel is caught, held inside the letters for your
in places the novel within the other letters
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: Emma is Jane Austen's novel

explanation.surface: A novel has caused a stir among the reader's own public.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to complain loudly and persistently, so the noun is a noisy clamour or outcry.

clue.text: Raised left side of base in girl's Victorian toy

parts.note: Zoe is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A girl's Victorian plaything has its left-hand base lifted up.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoetrope was a spinning drum with slits that made pictures appear to move, popular in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Bond stopping out for birthday

indicators.note: the bond stops up the other word, sitting inside it like a plug

parts.note: forth means out, as in go forth
a tie is a bond

explanation.surface: James Bond is grounded instead of heading out to celebrate his birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is simply a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially a fortieth is a fortieth birthday party, so the ordinal names the celebration.

clue.text: One after the other, as disputants may be

definitions.meaning: first meaning: consecutively, in a line
second meaning: ..., rhyming with cow, is having an argument

explanation.walkthrough: The same spelling is read two ways: row as a line, and row as a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: In a row means consecutively, while a row pronounced like cow is a quarrel, which arguing people are in.

clue.text: Stone block crushing state's defunct space hardware

indicators.note: the block crushes the state, holding it squeezed inside

parts.note: a slab is a block of stone
KY is the postal abbreviation of Kentucky, a US state

explanation.surface: A stone block falls on a state's obsolete space equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylab was the first American space station, launched in 1973 and fallen back to Earth in 1979.

clue.text: I work in Essen when picked up

definitions.text: I work in Essen when picked up

parts.words: I work in Essen when picked up
parts.note: Essen spoken aloud is the letters S and N, the chemical symbol of the metal this craftsman works

explanation.walkthrough: Essen looks like the German city, but said aloud it is 'S N', Sn, the symbol for tin; the worker in tin is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinsmith is a metalworker who makes and repairs things of tin, the element with symbol Sn.

clue.text: Duty dealt with by the FT?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a responsibility or burden
second meaning: ..., paid for by the newspaper itself

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer is what the Financial Times would say of a treat it pays for: 'on us'.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility; 'on us' is the phrase for something paid for by the speakers.

clue.text: Where to change old biker — menace, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs

parts.note: a rocker was a 1960s British motorcycle rider, rival of the mods
to loom is to threaten or menace

explanation.surface: An ageing motorcyclist threatens to change, as Spooner might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening R and L of ROCKER LOOM gives LOCKER ROOM. Rockers were leather-clad 1960s British bikers.
explanation.definitionFit: A locker room is where sports players or gym users get changed into kit.

clue.text: Core Attlee stirred?

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Was Clement Attlee's core support roused to action?
explanation.walkthrough: Attlee was the Labour Prime Minister swept in by the 1945 landslide; the voters stirred to back him are the answer, and the letters of the clue's first two words mixed give the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The electorate is the body of voters, the core that, roused, put Attlee into office.

clue.text: Similar characters offer hatred and bias freely

indicators.note: freely means without fixed order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Like-minded people express hostility and prejudice without restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of a feather, from the proverb about flocking together, are people of the same kind or tastes.

clue.text: Artist arrived secretly

parts.note: in came means arrived, as in 'in came the post'
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter turned up without anyone knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal Latin phrase for proceedings held in private, so it means privately or secretly.

clue.text: Bailiff dashed past, breaking up squabble

indicators.note: the scrambled letters break the squabble apart by sitting in its middle

parts.note: a tiff is a minor squabble

indicators.note: dashed means smashed, so the letters of past are rearranged

explanation.surface: A court officer rushes by to separate two people quarrelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed' turns PAST into PSTA, and 'breaking up' places that inside TIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a sheriff's or court officer, named after the metal-tipped staff carried as a badge of office.

clue.text: Councillor having viewed housing put back court's conclusion in recording of trial?

indicators.note: the participle for viewing houses the councillor, holding it inside

parts.note: seen is having viewed

indicators.note: back means turned around, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to put something is to set it

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: final letter of court

explanation.surface: A councillor who has watched a court case has its ending kept in a trial recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SET into TES; the last letter of court supplies T.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen test is a filmed audition, a recording made to try out a would-be actor, hence the question mark on trial.

clue.text: Bury old medic beneath hospital department?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the old medic sits beneath the department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a medical qualification and so a doctor

explanation.surface: A retired doctor is laid to rest under a ward.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place a body in a tomb, that is to bury it.

clue.text: Man and wife beset by depression

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the wife goes inside the depression

parts.note: a pan is a hollow or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: A husband and wife are both suffering from depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a husband beside 'wife', but it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the pieces are called men, and the pawn is the humblest of them.

clue.text: Hawk makes turn to pull up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: A hawk wheels round to pull out of a dive.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawk in politics is a militarist; a war dog is likewise someone eager for war.

clue.text: Old filmmaker, note, brought back yellow parrot

indicators.note: brought back means turned round, so the joined pieces are reversed

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French film director of the mid-twentieth century
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale
or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A veteran director returns with a yellow parrot in his film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrot' looks like a bird, but here it is someone who copies. Tati made the comic film Monsieur Hulot's Holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat mindlessly, so a parrot in this sense is a mimic or copier.

clue.text: Powder line inhaled by soaring jazz fan

indicators.note: the line is breathed in, taken inside the jazz fan
in a down clue, soaring means going up, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A high jazz lover snorts a line of powder.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into the fine powder used on skin.

clue.text: Volunteers to pack McIlroy's club

indicators.note: the golfer's name packs the volunteers, holding them inside

parts.note: Rory McIlroy is the Northern Irish golfer
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Helpers pack away a golf club belonging to Rory McIlroy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a golf club, but it is a service club.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotary is the international service organisation of local clubs for business people.

clue.text: Chief in China crossing border

indicators.note: the friend straddles the border, with it inside

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, a pal
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A leader in China crosses the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is rhyming slang, china plate standing for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal can mean first in importance, so it is a synonym of chief or principal.

clue.text: Calamity as sliver of glass found in fresh cat food

indicators.note: the letter is found inside the rearranged letters
fresh means new, so the letters are made into something new
a sliver is a tiny piece, the first letter of glass

explanation.surface: A disaster: a glass splinter turns up in a new tin of cat food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' makes ACTOFOD from CAT FOOD, and 'found in' puts G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An act of God is a natural disaster beyond human control, an insurance term for a calamity.
